features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.defect: No sign-off state exists in the product. A publish proceeds with zero sign-offs, and there is no surface on which to attach one.
features.evidence: Nothing records a sign-off, so nothing can require two. `grep -rin 'sign-?off|signoff|signOff'` over pkg/barn returns 9 hits and every one is either a CSS class (`verify__signoff`, `rc__signoffs`) or a computed sentence. The sentences say the opposite of the rule: screen 12 renders the literal string "You are the only reviewer on this Studio, so your decision is the decision." and screen 13's sign-off bar renders a criteria tally (observed: "2 of 4 met, 2 still to look at"). Approving on screen 12 calls commitExtension() (a git commit titled "Reviewed: N files"); recording on screen 13 writes a `## Verification` block into BRIEF.md. Neither writes a state any publish reads, and publishExtension() reads neither.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.defect: "Skip the brief" makes the required stage optional, erasing the distinction the flow map draws between stage 3 (main path, green) and stage 5 (explicitly optional). Separately: brief.vue's agree() pushes `query: { brief: '1' }` and editor.vue never reads it (`grep -i brief pages/editor.vue` matches nothing), so the brief is written to the pod but is never sent to the assistant as the first instruction, contrary to brief.vue's own comment that "the brief is not a ceremony, it is the prompt".
features.evidence: Half holds: the create route really does pass through the brief. Screen 02's only submit is "Draft the brief" (observed as the primary button), and submit() calls ensureExtension() then pushes BRIEF_ROUTE with prompt, outcome and placement in the query - so 02 -> 10 -> 03 is the path, and agree() writes BRIEF.md before pushing EDITOR_ROUTE. Half fails: the brief is exactly as skippable as screen 04. brief.vue renders a "Skip the brief" ghost button whose skip() pushes EDITOR_ROUTE with no BRIEF.md written, and the workspace is directly addressable at /barn/editor/:extension - screen 01's row menu "Open in the workspace" goes straight there. Nothing anywhere requires a brief to exist before building.

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.evidence: All five capabilities still reachable in the running Studio, checked one by one. CLI: the workspace's left pane has tabs Assistant / Files / Changes / Terminal, the Terminal being xterm on the pod's exec subresource. Raw output is one click from the activity stream - the stream's empty state renders an "Open the terminal" button, and clicking it made the terminal pane visible (measured height > 50px); the copy states it is still the source of truth ("the terminal below is the whole session, and the composer sends to it"). Files: the Files tab plus screen 05 at /barn/extensions/base/files, which rendered the tree and the contents of index.ts. GitHub import: "Import" on screen 01's masthead, "Import a repo instead" on screen 02, and "Import from GitHub" in the publish split's dropdown. Publish: "Publish" on the workspace masthead, enabled, with a dropdown of "Publish to GitHub / Import from GitHub / Remove local install". Settings: "Editor settings" opened the modal with the GitHub token field. Nothing the old build did has been removed.

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.defect: There is no way for a reviewer to write a comment, so nothing can be loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from. The author arrives back in the workspace with no record of what was asked for.
features.evidence: Half holds: "Request changes" on screen 12 exists, is enabled when there are changes, clears the deferral and routes the author to EDITOR_ROUTE for the same extension - the same workspace. Half is entirely missing: the reviewer's words never travel. There is no comment control anywhere on screen 12 (live text scan of /barn/review/base/working: hasComment false, hasSendToAssistant false), requestChanges() takes no argument and carries no query, and no review screen calls askAssistant() - `grep -rIn askAssistant` shows it called only from brief.vue ("what the assistant cannot decide"), review.vue (screen 04's "Ask about this file") and verification.vue ("Ask the assistant to check"). The decision bar on screen 12 is: "You are the only reviewer on this Studio, so your decision is the decision. Request changes | Come back to it | Approve and commit".

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: The review diff is against HEAD. Since a local publish never commits, HEAD and the last published version drift apart, and a reviewer of a published extension sees changes measured from the wrong point.
features.evidence: Half holds: it is one net diff, not a stream of intermediate edits. workingDiff() is `git add -A -N ; git diff HEAD` and fileDiff() is `git add -N -- <path> ; git diff HEAD -- <path>`, so a change made and undone before review contributes nothing by construction. Half fails: the baseline is the last commit, not the last published version. publishExtension() (the local install, the only publish that makes the extension installable here) builds and upserts a UIPlugin and never commits, so HEAD does not move when something is published. nodehealth is published as v0.1.0 - screen 01's "Running on" reads "catalog . v0.1.0" and its row menu offers "Remove the local install v0.1.0" - while its review diff is still measured against its last git commit. base's pod confirms the shape: HEAD is 8a704fb "The seeded extension" and `git diff HEAD --stat` gives "BRIEF.md | 34 ++++", which is exactly what screens 04 and 12 render. `grep -rIn 'lastPublished|last published'`: 0 hits, so no record of the published version exists to diff against.

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: Screen 09 does not exist. Connection state, permissions, access and data have no single home; the workspace strip and the settings modal show unrelated state; and the permission mode is an informational chip rather than a control, so nothing can be changed in one place and be true in the other.
features.evidence: Half holds: there is exactly one surface that edits the GitHub token - EditorSettingsModal.vue, the same component reused from screens 01, 03, 11 and 12 - so no second surface edits it. Everything else fails. There is no settings page: screen 09 has no route in index.ts, and "Editor settings" opens the bare modal the design says it replaces (observed content: "Editor settings / Used to import and publish extensions to GitHub. / GitHub token / Cancel / Save"). The strip on screen 03 and the modal are not the same state: the strip's label is computed as "Connected to this Rancher" (the Rancher session), while the modal's state is a GitHub token stored in a Secret. And there is no permission mode at all - the strip's chip is a non-clickable `data-testid="barn-permission-chip"` reading "Edits apply without asking", and AssistantPanel.vue's comment says why: the pod runs `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, so "there is no permission mode to switch to". `grep -rin permission` over pkg/barn finds no mode, setting or control.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Authored once on screen 10 and read as the same objects on screen 13. brief.vue's briefMarkdown() writes the heading `## How we will know it worked` followed by one `- [ ] <criterion>` per filled criterion; verification.vue's criteriaLines() reads sectionOf(brief, 'How we will know it worked') and takes every `- [ ]`/`- [x]` line, keyed on the criterion's own text. Verified live against real data: `kubectl -n barn exec deploy/barn-base-extension -- cat /app/pkg/base/BRIEF.md` holds four criteria, two ticked, and /barn/extensions/base/verification rendered exactly those four in the same order with the tally "2/4" and the two ticked ones already answered Yes. Walked against the running build: each row carries "Show me", which navigates the PreviewPanel (the extension's own dev server, framed on the right and reading "Loaded . just now") to the route the verdict was taken at, and the route is written back next to the verdict. Evidence is captured into the same file - the pod's BRIEF.md already contains the `## Verification` block with "- **Met**: ..." lines. I did not author a fresh criterion because BRIEF.md on the shared base pod is another verifier's working file; the write side and the read side use the identical heading and line syntax, and the round trip is observable on the existing four.

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: The Studio reimplements Banner, Card, Tabbed, Button, Modal, Badge and Menu as a private S-prefixed set instead of using the dashboard's, and screen 01 is a hand-rolled div grid rather than the Clusters page's SortableTable. The rule's claim that no new primitive is needed is true; the build does not honour it.
features.evidence: Half holds: nothing in the design needs a primitive the dashboard lacks - every shape used is a table, input, banner, card, tab or button. Half fails on the implementation the rule is checked against. The ten Studio pages are built on a bespoke 15-component set in pkg/barn/components/ui/ (SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar), whose own headers describe them as implementations of the Figma component sets rather than wrappers - SBanner "The design's Banner (Figma component set 4:51)", STabs "The design's Tab (Figma component set 4:34)". `grep -rn "from '@shell|from '@components" components pages` matches only the pre-redesign components (NewExtensionModal, ExtensionFiles, PublishStatus, ExtensionSelect, PublishSplit) and extension-starting.vue; no page under pages/ imports a dashboard component. Screen 01 in particular is not SortableTable: extensions.vue renders `<div class="studio-home__table">` with `<div class="studio-home__row">` children and its own COLUMNS array and sort comparators.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.defect: The snapshot is a manual action in the workspace, not a per-build automatic one, and screen 08 does not offer a rollback. A failure from a state nobody snapshotted has no way back.
features.evidence: Half holds: snapshots are real and work. extensions.ts has snapshot create (`git stash create` plus a tag so it survives), listSnapshots() and a restore, and EditorMasthead.vue exposes them as a "Snapshots" menu with "Take a snapshot" and a line per snapshot that opens a confirm before restoring. Observed on /barn/editor/base: the masthead carries "Snapshots" and "Undo". Half fails, and it is the word "guaranteed": no snapshot is taken automatically, so a failure only has a state to go back to if the author happened to take one first. `grep -n snapshot pages/build-failed.vue`: 0 hits, and live the failure screen's three ways back were "Fix it with the assistant", "See what changed", "Try the publish again" - no rollback offered at all. Nothing in publishTo() or publishExtension() snapshots before building.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Drove 01 (/barn/extensions), 02 (/barn/extensions/new), 10 (brief), 03 (/barn/editor/base), 04 (review), 05 (files) and 08 (build-failed, with a seeded sessionStorage failure) in one session. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no control disabled for a review reason appeared anywhere. A text scan of the workspace for approval / sign off / signed off / gate / OCI / registry / blocked returned []. The Publish button was enabled on screen 03 while the extension had unreviewed working-tree changes, and screen 02's "Draft the brief" submit was enabled. Two extensions created by other verifiers during this run (demo, v02-new-extension) went straight to Building with no approval step. I did not create one myself, per the shared-pod rule.

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.defect: There is no distribution boundary in the product. Publishing is local (build in the pod, upsert a UIPlugin) or a git push to refs/heads/main; neither is an OCI push and neither asks anybody. The one hard gate the whole flow map is organised around does not exist.
features.evidence: No code path gates any publish on anything. Greps over pkg/barn (excluding node_modules and extension-seed.generated.ts): `grep -rIiE '\boci\b'` 0 hits, `registry` 0, `ghcr` 0, `requiresApproval` 0, `blockPublish` 0, `approved` 0 (the 3 `canPublish` hits are all PublishGithubModal.vue's repo+token credential check). The two publish functions, publishExtension() and publishExtensionToGithub() in extensions.ts, are reached only through editor.vue publishTo(), whose sole precondition is `if (this.publishing) { return; }`, and the button is `:disabled="publishing"` and nothing else. Live: on /barn/editor/base, which had 1 unreviewed change and no sign-off recorded anywhere, `[data-testid="barn-publish-button"].disabled` read false, and a scan of the whole workspace page text for approval / sign off / gate / OCI / registry / blocked returned an empty list.

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.defect: Crossing the gate does not produce a PR, because there is no gate and the push is a direct push to main. The PR chip is a read of GitHub, not a record the product writes.
features.evidence: Half holds: screen 12 can display an existing PR. checkPullRequest() reads the pod's current branch, the stored token and the remembered repo, then calls findOpenPullRequest() and renders a chip that opens the PR, the repo's /pulls, settings or a retry depending on the state. Half fails: nothing in the product ever creates a PR. publishExtensionToGithub() commits and then runs `git push <remote> HEAD:refs/heads/main` - straight to main, no feature branch, no PR - so the chip's own precondition (a PR whose head is this extension's branch) can never be produced by the hand-off it is supposed to record. `grep -rIn 'pullRequest|pull request|\bPR\b'` over pkg/barn: 0 hits outside review-change.vue. Live on /barn/review/base/working the chip had nothing to say (no token configured, and no "pull request" text on the page).

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.defect: The preview is shared, not per-author, and no snapshot is taken per build. The publish boundary itself is sound.
features.evidence: Half holds and is genuinely enforced: preview and published are different objects and publishing is a separate deliberate act. The preview is the pod's dev server behind the apiserver service proxy; publishing runs build-pkg in the pod and upserts a UIPlugin, and nothing in the workspace touches that object. Observed on /barn/extensions: base has an edited working tree and reads "Running on: local (preview)" with "Remove the local install" disabled and annotated "not installed" - so all the editing done in its workspace has published nothing - while nodehealth reads "catalog . v0.1.0". Screen 11 states the same in words: "Everything here is still running only in its author's preview." Half fails on the rule's two qualifiers: it is not "yours alone" - the preview is one pod per extension at a fixed cluster URL that every Studio user sees, and I could watch other verifiers' edits to base appear in my session - and it is not "snapshotted per build", since snapshots are only ever taken by hand from the masthead menu.

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.defect: Per-hunk prompt provenance is not captured on screen 03 and therefore cannot arrive on screen 12. This confirms the screen-12 finding at its source: the data does not exist during authoring, so this is an authoring-side gap, not a review-side one.
features.evidence: The brief half survives; the prompt half is never captured at all, anywhere. Brief: screen 10 writes BRIEF.md into the pod's package, screen 12 reads it back into "The packet" (observed rendering the base brief's problem, who has it, what changes, non-goals and criteria) and screen 13 reads the same file. Provenance: nothing during authoring records which prompt produced which change. `grep -rIn provenance` over pkg/barn returns 7 hits, all in verification.vue about the line under a criterion, plus one unrelated comment in extensions.ts; `grep -rIn hunk` matches only DiffView.vue's patch parser and two comments. AssistantPanel.vue states the cause in its header: the activity stream is "Not real ... claude's output is a character stream, not a sequence of typed events, and turning one into the other is a parser nobody has written", and live the stream renders "The assistant runs in the terminal / This view will show each turn as steps with durations once the CLI's output is parsed into events." With no turn ever recorded there is nothing to attach to a hunk, and screen 12 shows no prompt (text scan for "prompt" on /barn/review/base/working: false).

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: Screen 01's per-row menu carries "Remove the local install", and it is live rather than aspirational. Opened all three row menus on /barn/extensions: nodehealth, which is published ("Running on: catalog . v0.1.0"), showed "Remove the local install v0.1.0" enabled; base and demo, which are not installed, showed it disabled with the reason "not installed". removeLocalInstall() resolves the plugin through packageIdentity() and DELETEs the UIPlugin in the cattle-ui-plugin namespace, which is the whole of what a local publish creates (upsertUiPlugin), leaving the pod and its tree untouched. Confirmed by reading rather than clicking - removing another verifier's install is destructive shared state. The GitHub push is not reversible from screen 01, but that is a push to someone else's repository rather than the "Live" state the map marks reversible.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes land back in the same workspace route. Screen 08: fixIt() and retry() both `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE, params: { extension } })` (retry adds `query: { publish: 'local' }`); seeChanges() goes to screen 04, which itself carries a "Back to assistant" button (observed in its button list). Verified live by loading /barn/extensions/base/build-failed with a seeded sessionStorage failure: the "Ways back" block rendered exactly "Fix it with the assistant", "See what changed", "Try the publish again". Screen 12: requestChanges() pushes EDITOR_ROUTE for the same extension. No recovery route leaves the product or opens a separate remediation surface.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: The packet is computed on demand at review time from whatever the working tree happens to hold, which is the opposite of the rule: an author who has not pushed is already in somebody's review queue, and nothing from earlier build cycles is retained (only the current uncommitted state exists).
features.evidence: Half holds: a packet is assembled and it is the right material. Screen 12's left column is titled "The packet" and carries BRIEF.md read from the pod, the file list grouped by directory, every file's diff and the live preview. Half fails, and it is the half the rule is about: nothing waits for a push and nothing is accumulated in the background. review-queue.vue builds the queue from the cluster on load - its own comment says "an extension with uncommitted changes in its pod is a change waiting on somebody" - via listExtensions + countChanges + readExtensionFile. Live at /barn/review with no push having happened anywhere: "Waiting on you 2", rows for base and nodehealth, and the page's own lede reads "Nothing in this list is live. Everything here is still running only in its author's preview". Screen 12 then re-reads changedFiles() and fileDiff() at open time.

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.defect: Scope drift is surfaced but not resolvable. The sign-off cannot accept the extra work into the brief or record that it should be removed, so the flag is a note rather than a decision point.
features.evidence: Half holds, and it is an honest half: screen 13 has a real Scope card that compares the build back to its own brief. It reads `## What we are deliberately not doing` out of BRIEF.md, extracts the non-goal terms (with a stop-list so common code words cannot fire it), scans only the added lines of the working diff, skips BRIEF.md itself, and has four states - unstated, nothing-changed, clear, drifted - listing term and files when it drifts. Half fails: there are no resolutions. The drifted branch renders a warning banner plus a static list of `term -> files` and nothing to press; there is no "accept it into the brief" and no "take it out" anywhere in verification.vue. Observed live on base: the card read "1 file changed / This change adds no lines outside the brief itself, so there is nothing to compare with what the brief ruled out", with no controls.

features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.

features.defect: There is no per-reviewer state and no incremental re-review. A reviewer returning after another push re-reads the whole working tree.

The only persisted review state is deferReview()/readDeferral(), which writes `git config --local barn.review.deferred <iso>` plus a note - one value per extension, not per reviewer, and it records "I am not ready", not "how much landed since I approved". Live: screen 11's rows carried only Deferred and Unsaved chips and no since-count banner; screen 12 had no filter control (text scan for "since your last look": false).

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people

features.defect: No identity is attached to either sign-off, so "is it safe?" and "does it work?" cannot be shown to have been answered by different people. Nothing distinguishes the developer from the person who asked, and nothing prevents one person doing both.
features.evidence: Half holds: screens 12 and 13 are two separate acts with two separate records, and signing one does not mark the other complete - 12's Approve calls commitExtension(name, 'Reviewed: N files'), 13's "Record the result" writes a `## Verification` block into BRIEF.md, and neither reads the other. Cross-checked in the pod with tmux capture-pane: the prompts were submitted and claude answered, so the replies exist and are simply not parsed into the stream. features.name: Discard every change
features.label: Discard all
features.promise: A button in the action bar throws away all three changed files at once.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Discard all' and confirm every changed file is reverted in the pod and the review screen empties or navigates away.
features.notes: Button/Ghost with icon/trash. Destructive; check for a confirmation.
features.defect: Discard does not remove intent-to-add files, it truncates them to 0 bytes and leaves them in the index, so they stay listed as changed for ever. 'git checkout -- .' restores an intent-to-add path from the empty blob in the index (git 2.39.5 in the pod - reproduced standalone in /tmp), and 'git clean' skips it because it is in the index. This is not a corner case: extensions.ts fileDiff() runs 'git add -N -- <path>' every time you open a file's diff, so merely LOOKING at a new file on this screen converts it to intent-to-add, and Discard then destroys its contents without removing it. Same for anything staged with real content (verified separately: unticking a 'git add'-ed file and pressing 'Discard 1' left it completely untouched, 35 bytes, still listed). Fix is to reset the named paths out of the index first, e.g. 'git reset -q -- <paths>' before the checkout+clean in discardChanges().
features.evidence: Drove it for real against a tree I had prepared (I first staged another verifier's BRIEF.md so a whole-tree checkout would restore it byte-identically instead of emptying it; its md5 75f1c293... was unchanged before and after, and I put its index entry back afterwards). Confirm read 'Discard all 5 changed files in base? This cannot be undone.'. The checkout half is real: CLAUDE.md's marker line was gone from the pod afterwards (grep -c VERIFY-04-REVIEW = 0). The clean half is real: two plain-untracked files (verify-04-review-discard.txt, verify-04-review-staged.txt) were removed from disk. HEAD stayed 8a704fb013061bc02d4a318e2f85404bef8c4665. BUT the screen did not empty: it came back reading 'These changes are running in your preview only. 2 of 2 files will be kept.', count badge 2, state badge still 'Unsaved', and verify-04-review-new.txt was still there at 0 bytes.

features.evidence: The handoff query is live and a publish really happens. Two observations. (1) The query is read and consumed: loading /barn/editor?publish=w1bogus left the URL as /barn/editor with the key stripped and no publish started, while a control key (/barn/editor?w1keep=1) survived untouched - so the stripping is specific to publish/brief. The shipped bundle (barn-0.5.22.umd.min.863.js) shows why: mounted() calls handleHandoff(), which reads $route.query.publish, $router.replace()s the query without publish and brief, and then calls publishTo(e) for 'local' or 'github'. (2) I drove it once, deliberately, to settle the rest: clicked 'Try the publish again' on the build-failed screen. It navigated to /barn/editor/base, stripped the key, and the publish ran to completion - the publish-status strip ended on 'base 0.1.0 installed' and kubectl showed a new UIPlugin, cattle-ui-plugin-system/base, plugin base v0.1.0. I removed that UIPlugin afterwards to put the environment back. features.promise: For every criterion the reviewer picks exactly one of three verdicts: Yes, No, or Can't tell.
features.howToVerify: Click each of the three segments on a criterion, confirm only one stays selected, that the selection colour matches (Yes green, No red, Can't tell grey), and that the progress chip and the footer message update.
features.notes: Segmented control repeated per criterion: 39:1232 (crit 1, Yes selected, #3E8C4F), 39:1257 (crit 2, Yes), 39:1284 (crit 3, No selected, #F64747), 39:1325 (crit 4, Can't tell selected, #F2F3F5 grey). Unselected segments are white. No 'unanswered' state of the control is drawn: every criterion in the mock carries a verdict.
features.evidence: Each criterion carries a three-segment group (role=group, aria-label 'Verdict for criterion N') with buttons Yes / No / Can't tell. Clicked each: aria-pressed=true moves to exactly one segment, fills are Yes rgb(62,140,79) green, No rgb(246,71,71) red, Can't tell rgb(201,162,39) amber. The footer sentence updated for each ('2 of 4 met, 1 not met, 1 could not be judged...'), and the masthead badge followed. There is a fourth state the design never draws: clicking the pressed segment again clears it back to unanswered (grey numbered badge, group gets --unanswered), which is also the state a criterion loads in, and it is counted and written separately ('still to look at' / 'Not looked at' in BRIEF.md) rather than being folded into Can't tell. All of it survived a save and reload.

features.name: Can't tell is a first-class, non-blocking verdict
features.label: Can't tell
features.promise: A criterion that can be neither passed nor failed is answered 'Can't tell': it is styled neutrally (grey, not red), it is excluded from the 'checked' count, its number badge stays a plain number rather than a tick or a cross, and it does NOT block publishing - only a 'No' does.
features.howToVerify: Set a criterion to 'Can't tell' and confirm three things: the counter does not increment, the footer still reports only the 'No' criteria as blocking, and the badge shows the criterion number in grey.
features.notes: Read from four drawn signals: the grey selected fill #F2F3F5 on 39:1330; the badge 39:1316 being a grey circle containing the literal '4' while badges 1-3 are icon glyphs on green/green/red; the counter saying '3 of 4 checked'; and 39:1313 saying 'Publishing is blocked while any criterion is No'. Criterion 4's evidence line explains why it cannot be answered: 'Nothing here has fifty nodes. Needs a real cluster.'
features.evidence: Set criterion 4 to Can't tell. The progress chip did not move (2/4 before and after). The badge kept the plain number '4'. The footer counted it separately from the failures: '2 of 4 met, 1 not met, 1 could not be judged.' It saved to BRIEF.md as '- **Could not tell** at `<route>`: <criterion>' - a state of its own, distinct from both the unticked box and 'Not looked at' - and came back selected after a reload. It does not block publishing, though neither does a No. Deviations: the fill and badge are warning amber (#C9A227) rather than the design's grey (grey is used for the unanswered state instead), and the 'only a No blocks' contrast cannot be observed because nothing anywhere blocks publishing - see 13-verify-blocked-note.
